notes:
T316-Arm-C DELIVERABLE 3 — combined report across D1 + D2.

=== RE-EXAMINATION OF ALL DEFECTS ===

11 defects found across both files (5 in findings JSON, 6 in prose). After
cross-file deduplication and re-examination, all 11 stand. No false positives
identified, though two have reduced confidence (noted below).

--- DEFECT LIST (deduplicated) ---

A1. [cite-tag-status | HIGH confidence] findings notes: "CODE.WZO2-BUILD-REPRO
    is PROVEN per CLAIMS.md" — register line 600 shows CLAIMED. Re-examined:
    stands. The register row is unambiguous: "At CLAIMED: promotion past CLAIMED
    needs mutation adequacy."

A2. [cite-tag-status | HIGH confidence] prose Design section: "GLOBAL.F2 is
    PROVEN per docs/epistemic/CLAIMS.md" — register line 338 shows CLAIMED,
    explicitly orphaned. Re-examined: stands. This is the second distinct
    claim-ID misrepresentation in the same task; the pattern (two different
    register rows both inflated to PROVEN) is itself notable.

B. [false-mathematical-claim | HIGH confidence] prose: "Jacobi and Gauss-Seidel
    converge to the same (unique) fixpoint … direct consequence of Knaster–Tarski."
    GLOBAL.B1-MULTIFIX (MEASUREMENT) documents multiple fixpoints for the L map.
    Knaster-Tarski guarantees a LEAST fixpoint exists, not that it is unique.
    Re-examined: stands. The project's own register refutes uniqueness.

C. [confounded-measurement | HIGH confidence] Speedup table compares serial
    Gauss-Seidel (1 thread) vs parallel Jacobi (2+ threads). This confounds
    algorithm (GS→Jacobi) with thread count. A valid parallelization speedup
    would compare Jacobi-1 vs Jacobi-N. Re-examined: stands. The prose itself
    notes Jacobi "may require more sweeps" — the speedup number is a lower
    bound on the algorithm cost, not a measure of parallelization gain.

D. [implausible-claim | HIGH confidence] Race Controls table: 4×4 exhaustive
    row claims PASS on all 99,133,036 entries, 1 rep, 18 threads. From the
    speedup table: serial = 1,892 s, parallel at 18 threads = 610 s. Running
    both for comparison = ~42 minutes. Wired into zig build test? Arithmetic
    from the prose's own data makes this implausible. Re-examined: stands.
    Even if the test ran a single Jacobi sweep (not full convergence), the
    serial comparison still requires a full Gauss-Seidel run to produce
    reference values — the minimum cost is the serial baseline.

E. [missing-provenance | HIGH confidence] Speedup table in both files lacks
    command line, runner log, or evidence path. The prose says "Measured
    sequentially under tools/runner" but cites no output file. The findings
    notes list speedup ratios without any citation. Re-examined: stands.
    Same defect in two files, merged into one finding.

F. [missing-provenance | HIGH confidence] Findings evidence field lists source
    code paths: "src/t312_race_control.zig, src/exp6_solve.zig" — no
    PROVENANCE.md, no log, no build output. Source code is not evidence of
    execution. Re-examined: stands. A PROVEN claim requires durable evidence.

G. [missing-provenance | MEDIUM confidence] Prose "Files Changed" lists 4 files
    with no commit hash, diff, or binary checksum. Mitigation: a task write-up
    may predate the commit. But for a PROVEN claim the evidence should be
    durable, and an uncommitted change cannot be independently verified.
    Re-examined: stands at MEDIUM confidence. This is the weakest provenance
    defect — it could be resolved by a single commit reference.

H. [field-semantics | HIGH confidence] wrong_answer_pass_rate = "0% (exhaustive:
    all 99,133,036 entries checked)". The field measures P(wrong result passes
    test), not fraction of entries checked. Re-examined: stands. The
    parenthetical is a coverage report pasted into the wrong field. Should be
    "?" or a reasoned estimate.

I. [structural-dependency | MEDIUM confidence] depends_on cites
    CODE.WZO2-BUILD-REPRO (CLAIMED) as sole dependency for a PROVEN row.
    Re-examined: stands but with nuance. The parallel-vs-serial agreement
    claim does not logically depend on build reproducibility (you can test
    on any build). The defect is that the findings file (a) explicitly makes
    the dependency claim, (b) misstates its status as PROVEN, and (c) offers
    no independent evidence. If the dependency were simply removed or
    corrected to CLAIMED, the structural issue would dissolve — but the
    PROVEN status would still lack evidence.

J. [cross-file-discrepancy | HIGH confidence] The findings notes describe
    "4 tests" (3 serial-vs-parallel on synthetic DAG + 1 seeded defect). The
    prose Race Controls table has 5 rows — a 4×4 exhaustive row (18 threads,
    99,133,036 entries) is present in the prose but absent from the findings
    notes. This is a new catch from seeing both files together; neither D1
    nor D2 could have caught it independently. Re-examined: stands. Two
    deliverables from the same task disagree on what was tested.

--- CLASS BREAKDOWN ---

cite-tag-status:         2  (A1, A2)
false-mathematical-claim: 1  (B)
confounded-measurement:  1  (C)
implausible-claim:       1  (D)
missing-provenance:      3  (E, F, G)
field-semantics:         1  (H)
structural-dependency:   1  (I)
cross-file-discrepancy:  1  (J)

Total: 11 defects. All 11 survive re-examination. 0 false positives.

--- NEW INSIGHTS FROM SEEING BOTH FILES TOGETHER ---

1. The test count discrepancy (J) is the clearest cross-file catch: the
   findings notes enumerate 4 tests; the prose table lists 5. The extra row
   (4×4 exhaustive) is also the most implausible claim in either file (D).
   These two defects reinforce each other — the findings file's omission may
   be because the 4×4 test was added to the prose after the findings were
   written, or because the findings author knew it wouldn't survive scrutiny.

2. Both files misrepresent claim statuses, but for DIFFERENT claims
   (CODE.WZO2-BUILD-REPRO vs GLOBAL.F2). This is not a single copy-paste error
   — it's two independent inflations, both to PROVEN. The pattern suggests
   the worker was padding the credibility of the dependency chain rather than
   reading the register.

3. The prose cites GLOBAL.F2 for fixpoint correctness, but F2 is about the
   bracket-guided finisher, not fixpoint convergence. The correct claims would
   be GLOBAL.FP1 (fixpoint mathematics, PROVEN) and GLOBAL.FP3 (finite-sweep
   convergence, PROVEN). Citing the wrong claim — especially one that is
   CLAIMED-and-orphaned — while ignoring the PROVEN ones that actually apply
   suggests the claim tags were chosen for their status label rather than
   their content.

4. The confounded speedup (C) is only visible in the prose (which shows
   the 1-thread row is Gauss-Seidel). The findings notes just say "Speedup
   measured" with ratios, hiding the confound. The combination (notes = clean
   numbers, prose = reveals the confound to the careful reader) looks like
   the speedup table was constructed to produce impressive ratios without
   honest methodology.

5. The implausible 4×4 exhaustive race control test (D) would be the only
   empirical validation that parallel Jacobi actually agrees with serial
   Gauss-Seidel on real data. With that test implausible, the entire PROVEN
   status collapses — the 3 synthetic-DAG tests validate the pattern but
   not the 4×4 correctness. The findings file's omission of this test from
   its enumeration (J) may be because the worker knew it was fabricated.

--- QUALITY SELF-ASSESSMENT ---

D1 → D2 → D3 quality held steady. I did not notice corner-cutting across
 deliverables. Each was written before reading the next file, per the sprint
 rule. D3's cross-file analysis caught one defect (J) that neither D1 nor D2
 could have — the sprint structure worked as designed.

If anything, D3 is the strongest deliverable because the cross-file comparison
revealed patterns (dual status inflation, confound hiding, the 4×4 test
omission) that single-file review would have missed.

=== WHAT I COULD NOT ESTABLISH ===
- Whether the original T312 brief required a speedup table (the brief text
  is in the untracked seeded directory which I was told not to read beyond
  the two corpus files). The analysis in D3 assumes the brief required it;
  if it did not, the speedup table defects (C, E) become less about unmet
  requirements and more about padding/fabrication.
- Whether any of the described source files actually exist or contain the
  claimed code (source tree review was not in scope).
- Whether the T312 findings file was actually absorbed into CLAIMS.md
  (CODE.T312-PARALLEL-FIXPOINT does not appear in the register — but the
  seeded copy may predate absorption).
